header.tolerance_rationale: 1e-8 relative: independent summation order across sezgi (Rust), the compiled C reference (C++), and opfunu (numpy) means bit-exactness is not expected from any of these pairings -- same value and same rationale cec2022_reference_values.json's header uses (M3-3 T8 precedent, mirrored here). In practice sezgi vs. the compiled C measures far tighter: max relative delta 2.906961657986538e-15 over all 240 probe points in this task's own generation run (near f64 machine epsilon), consistent with T2-T4's own ~1e-15 findings for their own, smaller, random-point fixtures.

probe_points.o: for fid 1-22: the official CEC2014 shift vector, first `dim` values of shift_data_<fid>.txt's single row. For fid 23-30 (composition): component 1's shift row (first `dim` values of shift_data_<fid>.txt's FIRST LINE) -- the same `x = comp_shift[0]` pin cec2014/mod.rs's own T4 module-doc section proves algebraically reduces to F_i* for every composition fid.
probe_points.random: python3 random.Random(20140101 + fid*100 + dim).uniform(-80.0, 80.0) drawn `dim` times -- one independent seeded draw per (fid,dim) combination, fully reproducible (points.py in this task's report). Absolute domain point (not offset from `o`), range [-80,80] comfortably inside the suite's [-100,100] domain -- same numeric range cec2022's own fixture used, base seed constant swapped from cec2022's 20220601 to this suite's own report-publication-year-styled 20140101.

header.dims: {10,30} only -- this milestone's vendored scope (cec2014/mod.rs module doc's 'Vendoring scope' section); the C itself also supports {2,20,50,100} but those dims were never vendored.

divergence_classes.opfunu-hybrid-shuffle-rotate-order: NEW for CEC2014 (same BUG CLASS M3-3 T8 already documented for opfunu's CEC2022 hybrids, tag 'opfunu-hybrid-shuffle-rotate-order' in cec2022_reference_values.json's header -- root cause recurs verbatim in this suite's own hybrid implementation, same codebase/author). opfunu 1.0.4's CEC2014 hybrid classes (F172014..F222014, fid 17-22) shuffle the SHIFT-ONLY vector and only THEN rotate: `z = x - self.f_shift; z1 = np.concatenate((z[self.idx1], z[self.idx2], z[self.idx3])); mz = np.dot(self.f_matrix, z1)` (opfunu/cec_based/cec2014.py, F172014.evaluate; F182014-F222014 share the identical z/z1/mz construction, only the component functions differ). The compiled C's hf01-hf06 rotate the WHOLE vector ONCE via sr_func (full shift+rotate) and only THEN shuffle the ROTATED result: `sr_func (x, z, nx, Os, Mr, 1.0, s_flag, r_flag); for (i=0; i<nx; i++) { y[i]=z[S[i]-1]; }` (quoted in full in cec2014/mod.rs's own T3 module-doc section, hf01 body). Permutation and matrix multiplication do not commute for a non-permutation-invariant rotation matrix, so opfunu's mz=M*(P*z) differs from the C's y=P*(M*z) on virtually every point with nonzero shift and a genuinely rotating matrix. Verified: fid 17 dim 10 'zeros' point: compiled C 33584263.05962241 vs opfunu 559730160.8611321 (rel=15.67, over 15x off; values match this fixture's stored c_value/opfunu_value for that point).
divergence_classes.opfunu-cf1-missing-shift-rotate: NEW (CEC2014-specific, fid 23 only). Composition Function 1's g2/g5 components (both report-named 'High Conditioned Elliptic Function F1'', ambiguous shared name -- cec2014/mod.rs's own T4 module doc records the code-over-report ruling: the C's cf01 rotates g2 via the outer r_flag parameter but hardcodes g5's r_flag literal to 0). opfunu's F232014.evaluate implements BOTH of these components by calling `operator.elliptic_func(x)` DIRECTLY on the raw (unshifted, unrotated) input `x` (opfunu/cec_based/cec2014.py lines 879 and 891: `g1 = self.lamdas[1] * operator.elliptic_func(x) + self.bias[1]` and `g4 = self.lamdas[4] * operator.elliptic_func(x) + self.bias[4]`) -- neither subtracts `self.f_shift[1]`/`self.f_shift[4]` nor applies any rotation, unlike every OTHER component in the same function (g0, g2, g3 each go through a properly-constructed sub-benchmark instance whose own `.evaluate(x)` correctly subtracts, and where applicable rotates, its own shift). Only the WEIGHT computation (`w1 = operator.calculate_weight(x - self.f_shift[1], ...)`, `w4 = ...` similarly) correctly uses the per-component shift -- the g_i VALUE itself does not, mirroring the shape (weight correct, g_i input wrong) of M3-3's CEC2022 'opfunu-composition-shift-o1' finding but with a DIFFERENT concrete defect (missing shift entirely, not merely the wrong component's shift). Verified via a diagnostic probe this task: `elliptic_func(x)` vs `elliptic_func(x - f_shift[1])` at a nonzero shift differ (0.0 vs 407057950.32 for a specific probed x and shift).
divergence_classes.opfunu-composition-wrong-submatrix: NEW (CEC2014-specific, fid 24-27; also compounds fid 29-30, see below). For these composition functions, opfunu builds each ROTATED component from a standalone single-function sub-benchmark instance (e.g. F242014's `self.g1 = F92014(self.ndim, None, self.f_shift[1], f_bias=0)`) WITHOUT overriding that sub-instance's own `f_matrix` constructor argument -- so the sub-instance loads its OWN standalone fid's DEFAULT rotation matrix file (F92014 defaults to `f_matrix="M_9_D"`, i.e. `M_9_D10.txt`/`M_9_D30.txt`) instead of the CALLING composition's own per-component BLOCK matrix (e.g. `M_24_D10.txt`'s rows `ndim..2*ndim`, the block the compiled C's cf02 actually multiplies that component by: `rastrigin_func(x,&fit[1],nx,&Os[1*nx],&Mr[1*nx*nx],1,r_flag)` -- cec2014/mod.rs's own T4 module doc quotes the same `&Mr[i*nx*nx]` per-component-block indexing pattern every `cf0N` shares). This is DISTINCT from CEC2022's 'opfunu-composition-shift-o1' (every component sharing component 0's SHIFT) -- here each component's SHIFT is correctly per-component (`self.f_shift[i]`, `check_shift_matrix` loads the full un-flattened per-component 2D block correctly for every CEC2014 composition function, including this class) -- only the ROTATION MATRIX is wrong. Verified via a diagnostic probe this task: F24's g1 (F92014) loaded matrix row `[0.6468, 1.2090, 0, 0, 0, ...]` while F24's OWN `f_matrix` rows `ndim..2*ndim` (the block the C actually reads for this component) are `[-0.3764, 0, 0, -0.0556, 0, ...]` -- genuinely different matrices. Composition Function 6 (fid 28, `F282014`) is the ONE composition class that does NOT have this bug: its `__init__` explicitly slices `self.f_matrix[i*ndim:(i+1)*ndim,:]` for EVERY one of its five components -- correspondingly, fid 28 is the only composition fid with ZERO measured disagreement against the compiled C in this task's fixture (all 8 points agree to well under 1e-8 relative).
divergence_classes.opfunu-hybrid-in-composition-shared-shuf: NEW (CEC2014-specific, fid 29-30 only, COMPOUNDS the two classes above). Composition Functions 7/8 (`F292014`/`F302014`) wrap three hybrid sub-instances (`F172014`/`F182014`/`F192014` for fid 29), each constructed with the SAME shuffle-file argument (`f_shuffle=f_shuffle`, i.e. `"shuffle_data_29_D"` passed to all three, `F292014.__init__`). Each sub-instance's own `check_shuffle_data` loads that file via `load_shift_data`, which calls `np.genfromtxt(...).reshape((-1))` -- flattening the ENTIRE file (`cf_num*dim` = 100 ints for D10, the same hardcoded-`cf_num=10`-sized loader convention `composition_shuffle_blocks`'s own doc comment records for the C reference's loader) into ONE 1D array, WITHOUT truncating to the first `dim` entries. Since each hybrid sub-instance's own index slicing (`self.idx1 = self.f_shuffle[:self.n1]`, etc.) only ever reads indices `< ndim` (<=30), all three sub-instances end up reading the SAME first `dim`-sized block (the block belonging to component 0 / hf01) regardless of which component (hf01/hf02/hf03) they actually represent -- verified via a diagnostic probe this task: `F29.g0.f_shuffle`, `.g1.f_shuffle`, `.g2.f_shuffle` are all IDENTICAL length-100 arrays. The compiled C's cf07/cf08 give each component its OWN `SS[i*nx]` shuffle block (cec2014/mod.rs's own T4 module doc: 'Each component gets its OWN FULL (Os[i*nx], Mr[i*nx*nx], SS[i*nx]) triple'). This compounds with `opfunu-hybrid-shuffle-rotate-order` (each of the three sub-instances ALSO has its own internal shuffle-before-rotate bug) and `opfunu-composition-wrong-submatrix` (each sub-instance ALSO uses its own standalone M_17_D/M_18_D/M_19_D matrix instead of a slice of the composition's own M_29_D/M_30_D) -- three independent bugs compounding for fid 29/30.
